chapter: New York 1930s and New Orleans expatriates
title: Clarinet registers, Crosby band and record identification
summary: Further talk of low-register clarinet, Dixieland trio choruses and a hazy record identification.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Who were the great clarinetists? Favorites and rivals

blocks.x: But I don't associate low register with shallow, good, and the northern clarinet chorus. Oh no, no, no, no, that's right.
That was a distinction, Dixieland kind of thing. Usually came in on the trio movement, one of these march type things.
Did you play much with Foss in bands with him? Never played with him, no, no, never.
You heard him with him? Plenty. With what, with big bands?

Who made the record of Wolverine Blues ever so flippin' with him? I don't recall. I can't remember that, about that time. Maybe that was Eddie Miller's number, but I still think some others. No, it doesn't ring the bell with me. No, there were some others too. Where he plays clarinet, I don't know. Some of the Mound City Blue Blowers, which were really kind of- I believe this was Bob Crosby.
The big band? The big band. The big band.
It could be South Rumpal Street Parade or something like that. I can't recall a fan. But what about guys like Perini? Who was he playing with to get along? He was starving to death at the time.
